Docket 1.3.81

**More findings that were wrong about real sites, now fixed.**

Docket has now been run against a published sample of 110 well-known websites,
and every serious finding it made was checked by hand against the pages. These
are the mistakes that turned up.

- *Whole reports built on something that was not the site.* When a site answered
  with a redirect page, a "prove you are human" check, or a notice that the page
  is not available in your region, Docket used to judge that stand-in as the
  site — one retailer drew 26 findings from a single redirect page. Those
  responses are now recognised, set aside, and reported for what they are; a
  crawl that reached nothing else says so instead of grading anything.
- *"Your homepage is set to noindex"* when your bare address redirects to a
  checkout or other host that is meant to be noindexed. The report now names
  the redirect, which is the thing to fix.
- *"Point both pages at one canonical URL"* for two versions of a site in the
  same language for different countries. That would drop one country from its
  own search results; the advice is now to link them with hreflang.
- *"Your pixel cannot fire"* when the pixel's ID was written without quotes.
- *"Almost no content"* on large pages built by JavaScript that Docket did not
  render — now reported as what the plain page contained, with the check to make.
- *AI search crawlers "blocked, may never have been a decision"* on a robots.txt
  that lists the crawlers it lets in and names some AI crawlers among them.
- *"No phone number anywhere on the site"* from a handful of pages that did not
  include a contact page. Findings about something missing now say how many
  pages were checked when the crawl did not see the whole site.
- *"Coming soon" as unfinished content* when it was part of a real sentence;
  *"robots.txt blocks your site from search engines"* stated as certain when
  Docket can only see the file it was sent.

**How Docket's crawler identifies itself.** Its user agent now links to a page
that explains what it requests and how to ask it to stay out, and it obeys any
robots.txt rule written for it by name.

99 checks across 13 areas.
